classification.difficultyReason: Directly apply the taught restricted-sample-space method: select the 60 mathematics students as the denominator and the 20 studying both as the numerator.

content.prompt: In a group of 100 students, 60 study mathematics, 50 study physics and 20 study both mathematics and physics. One of the mathematics students is selected at random. What is the probability that he also studies physics?

answer.worked:
The restricted sample space contains the 60 mathematics students, of whom 20 also study physics.

$$\begin{align*}P(\text{physics}\mid\text{mathematics})&=\frac{20}{60}\\P(\text{physics}\mid\text{mathematics})&=\frac{1}{3}\end{align*}$$
